papers.title: Prominent V Waves Augment Right Ventricular Afterload Independent of the Lung Vessels in Heart Failure: Implications for Clinical Assessment of Pulmonary Vascular Disease.
papers.summary: Among 1,069 HFpEF patients tested invasively, 21% had prominent V waves (PAWP V ≥10 mm Hg above mean). They had worse LA myopathy, higher PA systolic pressure (54 vs 38 mm Hg), more RV dysfunction, and adjusted HR 2.09 for HF hospitalization or death. V-wave correction reduced apparent combined PH from 60% to 29%.
papers.short_title: prominent V waves and right ventricular afterload in HFpEF
